summary:
Meristellas Space Mission is a Roblox game where students prepare for and run a lunar science outpost, and every choice is a trade-off. In an Earth lab they pick a mission, Water Ice Survey or Rocks and Minerals, then pack gear from an Equipment Vault. Real rockets can only carry so much weight, so the backpack has just 7 slots. Each tool either uses or makes “power points”, and a live power meter shows whether the plan adds up. Solar Panels make 4, but the Moon’s two-week night shuts them down, so players must weigh a Battery against another tool. Forget required gear, such as the Water Extraction Heater, and the mission suffers on the Moon.

The game makes these decisions tangible instead of abstract. Kids see the consequences of their choices in the power meter and the mission itself, and short fun facts and item explanations keep the language simple and the pace fun.

It matters because it shows how mission planning depends on limited power and weight, and it builds early engineering judgment.
details:
Meristellas Space Mission is a Roblox game where students prepare for a Moon science mission. In an Earth lab they pick a mission (Water Ice Survey or Rocks and Minerals), get briefed by a scientist, and pack gear from an Equipment Vault. The backpack has only 7 slots, and every tool uses or makes power points, shown on a live power meter. After a rocket launch, they carry out the mission on the Moon, where missing gear and the long lunar night, which shuts down solar panels, cause real problems.

Benefits and impact: Students experience trade-offs like weight limits, power budgets and planning ahead, instead of just reading about them. Kid-friendly item explanations, fun facts and a built-in guide keep it simple and fun, with the aim of building early engineering judgment.

Tools: Roblox Studio and Luau, using Roblox’s built-in UI, sound and animation systems, with an AI assistant helping edit scripts.

Creativity: There’s no perfect loadout. Solar panels make the most power but fail at night, so players must choose between a battery and another tool. Cutscenes, a character-led briefing and a jolly space soundtrack make planning feel like an adventure.

Factors considered: Age-appropriate language, help available on request (G key or “?” button, mobile-friendly), a clear screen layout, and balance so required gear always fits.
